{{Short description|American mathematician and historian of mathematics (b. 1947)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date = December 2025}}
{{Use American English|date = December 2025}}

'''William Wade Dunham''' (born 1947) is an American [[scientific writing|writer]] who was originally trained in [[topology]] but became interested in the [[history of mathematics]] and specializes in [[Leonhard Euler]]. He has received several awards for writing and teaching on this subject.<ref name=passhema>{{cite web
|url=http://www.passhema.org/past-conferences/2002/sshema/Dunham2.html
|title=William Dunham
|publisher=www.passhema.org
|accessdate=2008-06-15
|archive-date=2016-10-30
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161030065508/http://www.passhema.org/past-conferences/2002/sshema/Dunham2.html
|url-status=dead
}}</ref>

==Education==
Dunham received his bachelor's degree from the [[University of Pittsburgh]] in 1969, his master's degree from [[Ohio State University]] in 1970, and his PhD from the same institution in 1974.<ref name="Mathematics Genealogy Project">{{cite web | title=William Dunham | website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project | url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=10022 | access-date=2022-11-13}}</ref>

==Writings==
Dunham  won the American Association of Publishers' award for writing  the Best Mathematics Book of 1994 for his book ''The Mathematical Universe''.<ref name=passhema/> In his book ''Euler: The Master of Us All'', he examines Leonhard Euler's impressive mathematical work.<ref>
{{cite book
|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uKOVNvGOkhQC&q=William+Dunham
|title=Euler: The Master of Us All - Google Book Search
|accessdate=2008-06-15
|last=Dunham
|first=Willam
|date=4 March 1999
|publisher=Cambridge University Press
|isbn=9780883853283
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Wagner, Clifford|title=Review of ''Euler: The Master of Us All'' by William Dunham|website=Mathematical Association of America|date=July 2007|url=http://www.maa.org/publications/periodicals/convergence/euler-the-master-of-us-all}}</ref> He received a [[Lester R. Ford Award]] in 2006 for his expository article ''Touring the Calculus'',<ref>{{cite journal|author=Dunham, William|title=Touring the Calculus|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|year=2005|volume=112|pages=1–19|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/touring-the-calculus-gallery|doi=10.2307/30037380|jstor=30037380}}</ref> and the [[Chauvenet Prize]] in 2022 for his article on the [[Möbius function]].<ref name="Dunham 2018 pp. 83–91">{{cite journal | last=Dunham | first=William | title=The Early (and Peculiar) History of the Möbius Function | journal=Mathematics Magazine | publisher=Taylor & Francis | volume=91 | issue=2 | date=2018-03-15 | issn=0025-570X | doi=10.1080/0025570x.2017.1413921 | pages=83–91| s2cid=125148213 }}</ref>

In 2007, Dunham gave a lecture about  Euler's product-sum formula and its relationship to [[analytic number theory]], as well as discussed Euler's evaluation of a non-trivial integral at the celebration of "Year of Euler" by the [[Euler Society]].<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.maa.org/news/070907mfhighlight.html
|title=MathFest Highlight: William Dunham Presents Euler in Three Acts
|publisher=www.maa.org
|accessdate=2008-06-15}}</ref> He published a chapter "Euler and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra" in the book ''The Genius of Euler'' published in 2007 to commemorate  the 300th birthday of Euler.<ref>
{{cite book
|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=M4-zUnrSxNoC&q=William+Dunham
|title=The genius of Euler: reflections on ... - Google Book Search
|accessdate=2008-06-15
|last=Dunham
|first=William
|year=2007
|isbn=9780883855584
}}
</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Bradley, Rob|date=25 February 2007|website=Mathematical Association of America|title=Review of ''The Genius of Euler'' edited by William Dunham|url=http://www.maa.org/publications/maa-reviews/the-genius-of-euler-reflections-on-his-life-and-work}}</ref>
